backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior, residual target and featurize unchanged. In the CatBoostRegressor call, set border_count=32 (default is 254) and max_bin=32, and keep depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations, MAE loss and the seed. Coarser quantisation of the continuous RDKit descriptors acts as an implicit regulariser and reduces the search space of splits, which the prior work did not try. Only the quantisation changes.
backlog.title: Coarse feature quantisation with bounded border count

backlog.spec: Replace the four-term OLS prior with a Ridge model fitted on all standardised RDKit descriptors from Descriptors.descList (replace nan and inf with 0, drop zero-variance columns using training statistics only, then standardise using training means and sds). Choose the ridge alpha from {1, 10, 100, 1000} by a 3-fold inner split on the training molecules using a grouped split on Murcko scaffolds. Fit CatBoost MAE on the residual of this prior, and keep the rest of the pipeline the same. This gives a smooth linear baseline over the full descriptor set, and it is not the stacking or feature-appending approach that was rejected before.
backlog.title: Ridge prior on all standardised RDKit descriptors instead of the four-term OLS

backlog.spec: Add a normalisation step applied inside both featurize() and base_features() before descriptors are computed. For each SMILES, parse the molecule, keep only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count using Chem.GetMolFrags(mol, asMols=True), then neutralise the common charged groups with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger (fall back to the raw molecule if any step fails or returns None). Featurise the cleaned molecule instead of the original. Counterions and recorded salt forms add fingerprint bits and distort MolWt, TPSA and MolLogP, which the OLS prior depends on directly, so this is a cleanup of the inputs rather than a new feature block. Keep the model, prior and all hyperparameters identical.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and charge neutralisation before featurisation

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and CatBoost MAE residual setup. Change only the CatBoost hyperparameters: DEPTH=4, ITERS=1500, LR=0.03, and add l2_leaf_reg=6. Everything else stays unchanged.
backlog.title: CatBoost depth/lr/iterations tuning on residual

backlog.spec: Replace the single four-term OLS prior with the simple average of four separate least-squares priors, each fitted on its own small descriptor subset of the training fold: (a) TPSA and MolLogP, (b) MolWt and NumRotatableBonds, (c) NumHDonors and NumHAcceptors, (d) MolLogP, TPSA and FractionCSP3. Each prior has an intercept and is fitted with np.linalg.lstsq as now; the prior prediction for any molecule is the mean of the four. Fit CatBoost MAE on the residual of this averaged prior and add the averaged prior back at prediction time, exactly as the current code does with its single prior. Averaging low-variance priors over overlapping descriptor subsets is more stable on unseen scaffolds than one four-term fit, and the prior is the part of the model that extrapolates.
backlog.title: Average several small linear priors instead of one OLS

backlog.spec: After computing the final prediction (CatBoost residual plus the OLS prior term), clip it elementwise to the interval [min(train_y), max(train_y)] using np.clip before returning. Permeability values in this benchmark live in a bounded log range, the folds test on unseen scaffolds, and the additive OLS-prior-plus-residual construction can extrapolate past the data range for odd molecules; clipping removes exactly those large one-sided errors that dominate a mean-absolute-error score. This is a two-line change that touches nothing else in the pipeline.
backlog.title: Clip predictions to the observed training range

backlog.spec: Keep everything in the incumbent train.py and add only CatBoost leaf regularisation: pass l2_leaf_reg=10.0 (the default is 3.0) to the CatBoostRegressor constructor, along with the existing loss_function='MAE', depth, learning_rate, iterations, random_seed, verbose and thread_count arguments. Nothing else changes: same features, same OLS prior, same residual target. This is a pure shrinkage test on the leaf values and is the untried regularisation axis for this model; if it helps, l2_leaf_reg=20 is the natural follow-up.
backlog.title: Stronger leaf regularisation for the residual CatBoost

backlog.spec: At the top of fit_predict, canonicalise each training SMILES via Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and collapse duplicate canonical strings into one row whose target is the mean of the duplicates' train_y values (keep the first SMILES of each group as the representative). Fit both the OLS prior and the CatBoost residual model on the deduplicated set; predict the test molecules unchanged. Measured permeability sets often contain repeated structures and stereo-variant or tautomer-duplicate entries, which silently upweight those molecules and inflate the effective sample at a few points; averaging their labels removes that duplication without discarding information. Report how many rows are dropped so the effect can be judged.
backlog.title: Deduplicate identical molecules with label averaging

backlog.spec: At the start of fit_predict, canonicalise each training SMILES (Chem.MolToSmiles of the parsed molecule) and collapse duplicate canonical structures into a single training row whose target is the mean of the duplicates' values; build the OLS prior and fit CatBoost on this deduplicated set. Public permeability tables commonly contain the same structure under different SMILES strings or salt forms, and duplicates both double-count those molecules in the MAE objective and leak repeated structures across the scaffold folds. Leave the test path untouched. Report nothing extra; the change should be a short helper that returns the reduced smiles list and target array.
backlog.title: Deduplicate identical molecules with averaged labels

backlog.spec: Train two CatBoost MAE residual models. Model A uses the current features. Model B uses only MACCS keys plus the RDKit descriptors, with no Morgan bits. Average the two predictions with equal weight and add the OLS prior.
backlog.title: Equal-weight blend of CatBoost with MACCS-only CatBoost

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Compute for each molecule its generic Murcko scaffold SMILES (MurckoScaffold.MakeScaffoldGeneric on GetScaffoldForMol, then MolToSmiles) and its sorted ring-system count string. Append these two strings as categorical columns to the numeric feature matrix and pass their column indices through cat_features in CatBoostRegressor, so CatBoost uses its ordered target statistics. Use a fixed string-to-int mapping built only from the training molecules, with unseen test strings mapped to a missing-value token. This is a categorical encoding of scaffold identity, which the scaffold-grouped folds never share across folds.
backlog.title: Murcko scaffold and ring-system strings as CatBoost categorical features

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior on the four descriptors. Let h be the heavy-atom count of each training molecule (Chem.Lipinski.HeavyAtomCount, clipped below at 1). Fit the OLS prior as before, then form the target r = (y - prior) / sqrt(h) and fit the CatBoost MAE model on r. At prediction time multiply the CatBoost output by sqrt(h_test) and add the prior. This puts the residual on a per-size scale, so large molecules with bigger residuals no longer dominate the MAE leaf updates. Keep all CatBoost settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-scaled residual target

backlog.spec: Train 5 CatBoost MAE models on the OLS residual with seeds seed*10+i (i=0..4), 500 iterations each at depth 6 and lr 0.07, thread_count=8. Average their residual predictions and add the OLS prediction. Keep features unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged CatBoost residual model

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the residual target. In the CatBoostRegressor call, add langevin=True and diffusion_temperature=1000 (keep MAE loss, depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations, random_seed=seed). Stochastic gradient Langevin boosting adds noise to the leaf and gradient updates as a regulariser, which is a different mechanism from the rsm and subsampling tried before. If the MAE loss rejects langevin, fall back to the same settings with loss_function='Quantile:alpha=0.5'.
backlog.title: Langevin (SGLB) boosting for the residual CatBoost model

backlog.spec: Keep the current pipeline exactly (OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP, CatBoost MAE on the residual, Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors) and only change the boosting hyperparameters: set DEPTH=4, LR=0.02 and ITERS=3000. The notes say depth/learning-rate/iteration tuning on the residual setup is untried, and with 728 molecules and ~2250 features a shallower tree with a longer, slower path is the standard fix for a boosting model that has plateaued. Change nothing else; no new features, no new model family. Keep random_seed=seed and thread_count=8. Runtime should stay well inside the 10-minute budget (the current job is far below it), but if it is close, drop ITERS to 2000.
backlog.title: Shallower, slower CatBoost on the residual

backlog.spec: Set CatBoost boosting_type='Ordered', l2_leaf_reg=10, depth 6, and random_strength=2. Keep MAE loss, the OLS residual target and 800 iterations.
backlog.title: Ordered boosting with strong L2

backlog.spec: Keep the existing OLS prior on TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and MolLogP and the CatBoost MAE model fitted on the residual. Change only the CatBoost settings: depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, iterations=1500, l2_leaf_reg=10, random_strength=1.0. Leave featurize, the prior and the seed handling unchanged. This is the untried tuning direction named in the notes, so it targets the depth, rate, iteration and L2 trade-off that the current settings (depth 6, lr 0.05, 800 iterations) have not explored.
backlog.title: CatBoost residual hyperparameter sweep (shallower, more regularised)

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Train two CatBoost MAE models on the same residual: one with depth 4 and 1000 iterations, one with depth 8 and 500 iterations, both at lr 0.05 with seeds seed and seed+1. Average their predictions with equal weight before adding the prior. This is a small deterministic depth-diverse ensemble, distinct from the random-subspace bag and the median-aggregated depth bag already tried, and it uses only the two existing settings with no new features.
backlog.title: Two-seed-pair CatBoost bag with differing depths

backlog.spec: Augment the training set with one extra copy of the feature matrix. Add Gaussian noise with sd 0.05 times each column's std to the descriptor columns only, not the fingerprint columns. Keep the same residual targets. Fit CatBoost on the doubled data, using the seed for the noise.
backlog.title: Gaussian descriptor jitter augmentation

memo: Helped: compact descriptors (MACCS 0.4096 vs 0.4417 baseline), CatBoost MAE loss (0.3837), and an OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP with CatBoost fit on residuals (0.3757 and 0.3664; incumbent mean_adjusted 0.3711). Did not help: Morgan counts (0.4451), Tanimoto kernel ridge (0.4357), MLP (0.4734), LightGBM l1 (0.3882), stacking (0.3904), PCA (0.3893), torsion counts (0.3771), 3D shape (0.3780), ElasticNet (0.3840), monotone constraints (0.3869), ionisation SMARTS (0.3764), local linear prior (0.3886), Nystroem prior (0.3915). Within noise (sd about 0.0037): residual refinements (0.3718, 0.3716), scaffold weighting (0.3724), median prior (0.3726), pruning (0.3728). Best recent: two-phase Huber then MAE boosting (0.3701), only -0.0010 vs incumbent, so likely noise. Plateau: extra features, model swaps and target tricks lose. Next: tune CatBoost depth, learning rate, iterations and l2 on the residual setup, which is untried, and seed-average CatBoost. Replicate anything near 0.37. Avoid family swaps and feature stacking.
